subject: Follow-up: throughput & latency discovery — next steps

Subject: Follow-up: throughput & latency discovery — next steps

Hi Priya / Markus,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — really useful to hear about Nimbus Health's batch inference patterns for clinical summarization. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

- Key takeaways from today
  - Typical request: document-level summaries, average input length ~1,800 tokens, 95th percentile ~4,200 tokens.
  - Peak concurrency during end-of-day processing windows: ~240 concurrent requests over a 20-minute window.
  - Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 400ms for API responses during interactive usage; batch window throughput target ~10k docs/hour.

- What we propose next
  1) Technical deep dive / capacity-sizing session (30–45m) to map those workload numbers to a Dedicated GPU pool configuration (batching, KV cache strategy, and quantization tradeoffs).
  2) We'll bring a short workload snapshot template for you to drop in real telemetry (I've attached an example CSV).
  3) After the call we can produce a recommended config (GPU types, pool size, autoscaling policy) and a draft cost estimate.

Can we lock a slot for a capacity-sizing workshop next week? Here are a few options in PST:
- Tue 11/10: 10:00–10:45 or 15:00–15:45
- Wed 11/11: 09:00–09:45

If those don't work, share two slots that do and Rohan (our solutions engineer) will take the lead on the deep dive.

Attachments: nimbus-workload-snapshot.csv (example), redwood-demo-ops.pdf (short ops runbook)

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0143

Two quick clarifications for the workshop so Rohan comes prepared:
- We use mixed workloads (interactive + batch). For the workshop please consider a hybrid strategy: keep 4–6 smaller instances for low-latency interactive traffic and a scalable pool for batch spikes.
- Our compliance team will want to confirm options for private deployments; for this session it's fine to focus on sizing and latency tradeoffs.
